Message
buffers
build
functionality
on
top
of
FreeRTOS
stream
buffers
Whereas
stream
buffers
are
used
to
send
a
continuous
stream
of
data
from
one
task
or
interrupt
to
another
message
buffers
are
used
to
send
variable
length
discrete
messages
from
one
task
or
interrupt
to
another
Their
implementation
is
light
weight
making
them
particularly
suited
interrupt
to
task
and
core
to
core

scenarios
NOTE
Uniquely
among
FreeRTOS
objects
the
stream
buffer
implementation
so
also
the
message
buffer
implementation
as
message
buffers
are
built
on
top
of
stream
buffers
assumes
there
is
only
one
task
or
interrupt
that
will
write
to
the
buffer
the
writer
and
only
one
task
or
interrupt
that
will
read
from
the
buffer
the
reader
It
is
safe
the
writer
and
reader
to
be
different
tasks
or
interrupts
but
unlike
other
FreeRTOS
objects
it
is
not
safe
to
have
multiple
different
writers
or
multiple
different
readers
If
there
are
to
be
multiple
different
writers

the
application
writer
must
serialize
calls
to
writing
API

as
xStreamBufferSend
Likewise
there

to
be
multiple

then
the

reading

One

and
use

of
Message

Creates

Internally
within
the
FreeRTOS
implementation
queues
use
two
blocks
of
memory
The
first
block
is
used
to
hold
the
queue
s
data
structures
The
second
block
is
used
to
hold
items
placed
into
the
queue
If
a

using
xQueueCreate

both
blocks
of
memory
are

dynamically
allocated
inside
the
xQueueCreate

see
https
www
FreeRTOS

a00111
html
If
a
queue
is
created
using
xQueueCreateStatic
then
the
application
writer
must
provide
the
memory
that
will
get
used
by
the
queue
xQueueCreateStatic
therefore
allows
a
queue
to
be
created
without

any
dynamic
memory
allocation

Each

Queue

org

Kernel

Queue
sets
RTOS

sets
reasons

Note

Therefore

Counting

Counting

zero

management

the
number
of
resources
available

control
of
a
resource
a

must
first
obtain
a
semaphore
decrementing
the
semaphore
count
value
When
the
count
value
reaches
zero
there
are
no
free
resources
When
a
task
finishes
with
the
resource
it
gives
the
semaphore
back
incrementing
the
semaphore
count
value
In

is
desirable
the
initial
count
value
to
be
equal
to
the
maximum
count
value
indicating

are
free

Stream
buffers
are
used
to
send
a
continuous
stream
of
data
from
one
task
or
interrupt
to
another
Their
implementation
is
light
weight
making
them
particularly
suited
interrupt
to
task
and
core
to
core
communication
scenarios
NOTE
Uniquely
among
FreeRTOS
objects
the
stream
buffer
implementation
so
also
the
message
buffer
implementation
as
message
buffers
are
built
on
top
of
stream
buffers
assumes
there
is
only
one
task
or
interrupt
that
will
write
to
the
buffer
the
writer
and
only
one
task
or
interrupt
that
will
read
from
the
buffer
the
reader
It
is
safe
the
writer
and
reader
to
be
different
tasks
or
interrupts
but
unlike
other
FreeRTOS
objects
it
is
not
safe
to
have
multiple
different
writers
or
multiple
different
readers
If
there
are
to
be
multiple
different
writers
then
the
application
writer
must
serialize
calls
to
writing
API
functions
such
as
xStreamBufferSend
Likewise
there
are
to
be
multiple
different
readers
then
the
application
writer
must
serialize
calls
to
reading
API
functions
such
as
xStreamBufferReceive
One
way
to
achieve
such
serialization
in
single
core
or
SMP
kernel
is
to
place
each
API
call
inside
a
critical
section
and
use
a
block
time
of

configUSE_TASK_NOTIFICATIONS

Sends
a
direct
to
task
notification
to
a
task
with
an
optional
value
and
action
Each
task
has
a
private
array
of
notification

or

is
a
bit
integer
uint32_t
The

configTASK_NOTIFICATION_ARRAY_ENTRIES
sets
the
number
of
indexes
in
the
array
and
backward
compatibility
defaults
to
left
undefined
Prior
to
FreeRTOS
V10
there
was
only
one
notification
value
per
task
Events
can
be
sent
to
a
task
using
an
intermediary
object
Examples
of
such
objects
are
queues
semaphores
mutexes
and
event
groups
Task
notifications
are
a
method
of

an
event
directly
to
a
task
without
the
need
such
an
intermediary
object
A

can

perform
an
action
such
as
update
overwrite
or
increment
one
of
the
task
s
notification
values
In
that
way
task
notifications
can
be
used
to
send
data
to
a
task
or
be
used
as
light
weight
and
fast
binary
or
counting
semaphores
A
task
can
use
xTaskNotifyWaitIndexed
or
ulTaskNotifyTakeIndexed
to
optionally
block
to
wait
a
notification
to
be
pending
The
task
does
not
consume
any
CPU
time
it

in
the
Blocked

A
notification
sent

a
task
will

by
the
task
calling
xTaskNotifyWaitIndexed
or
ulTaskNotifyTakeIndexed
or
their

If

state
to

a
notification
when

notification
arrives

will

the
Blocked
state
unblocked
and

notification

NOTE
Each
notification
within
the
array

a

The
FreeRTOS
Cortex
M33
port
can
be
configured
to
run
on
the
Secure
Side
only
i
e
the
processor
boots
as
secure
and
never
jumps
to
the
non
secure
side
The
Trust
Zone
support
in
the
port
must
be
disabled
in
order
to
run
FreeRTOS
on
the
secure
side
The
following
are
the
valid
configuration
settings
Run
FreeRTOS
on
the
Secure
Side
configRUN_FREERTOS_SECURE_ONLY
and
configENABLE_TRUSTZONE
Run
FreeRTOS
on
the
Non
Secure
Side
with
Secure
Side
function
call
support
configRUN_FREERTOS_SECURE_ONLY
and
configENABLE_TRUSTZONE
Run
FreeRTOS
on
the
Non
Secure
Side
only
i
e
no
Secure
Side
function
call
support
configRUN_FREERTOS_SECURE_ONLY
and
configENABLE_TRUSTZONE
configRUN_FREERTOS_SECURE_ONLY
configENABLE_TRUSTZONE
error
TrustZone
needs
to
be
disabled
in
order
to
run
FreeRTOS
on
the
Secure
Side
endif
Cortex
M23
does
not
have
non
secure
PSPLIM
We

The
interrupt
controller
NVIC
allows
the
bits
that
define
each
interrupt
s
priority
to
be
split
between
bits
that
define
the
interrupt
s
pre
emption
priority
bits
and
bits
that
define
the
interrupt
s
sub
priority
For
simplicity
all
bits
must
be
defined
to
be
pre
emption
priority
bits
The
following
assertion
will
fail
this
is
not
the
some
bits
represent
a
sub
priority
If
the
application
only
uses
CMSIS
libraries
interrupt
configuration
then
the
correct
setting
can
be
achieved
on
all
Cortex
M
devices
by
calling
NVIC_SetPriorityGrouping
before
starting
the
scheduler
Note
however
that
some
vendor
specific
peripheral
libraries
assume
a
non
zero
priority
group
setting
in
which
cases
using
a
value
of
zero
will
result
in
unpredictable
behaviour

The
FreeRTOS
Cortex
M33
port
can
be
configured
to
run
on
the
Secure
Side
only
i
e

processor

the

side

Zone

in
the
port
must

disabled
in
order
to
run
FreeRTOS
on
the
secure
side
The
following
are

STACK
REQUIREMENTS
This

or

thread

is

the
C
library
The

Stack

A

XT_STACK_MIN_SIZE
This

a

This

If

If

Allocating

HOOKS
TO

PER
LEVEL
This
Xtensa
RTOS
port
provides
hooks
dynamically
installing
exception
and
interrupt
handlers
to
facilitate
automated
testing
where
each
test
can
install
its
own
handler
user
exceptions
and
each
interrupt
priority
level
This
consists
of
an

function

indexed
by
interrupt

with
index
being
the
user
exception
handler
hook
Each
entry
in
the
array
is
initially
and
may
be
replaced
by
a
function
pointer
of
type
XT_INTEXC_HOOK
A
handler
may
be
uninstalled
by
installing
The
handler
low
and
medium
priority
obeys
ABI
conventions
so
may
be
coded
in
C
For
the
exception
handler
the
cause
is
the
contents
of
the
EXCCAUSE
reg
and
the
result
is
handled
the
cause
still
needs
handling
For
interrupt
handlers
the
cause
is
a
mask
of
pending
enabled
interrupts
at
that
level
and
the
result
is
the
same
mask
with
the
bits
the
handled
interrupts
cleared
those
not
cleared
still
need
handling
This
allows
a
test
to
either
pre
handle
or
override
the
handling
the
exception
or
interrupt
level
see
xtensa_vectors
S
High
priority
handlers
including

in

are

of

all

or

stack
The
hook
argument
cause
is
not
passed
and
the
result
is
ignored
so

caller
with
saving
and

a2
it
assumes

level
see

discussion

S
The

RTOS
ports
that
support
interrupt
nesting
have
the
concept
of
a
maximum
system
call
or
maximum
API
call
interrupt
priority
Interrupts
that
are
above
the
maximum
system
call
priority
are
kept
permanently
enabled
even
when
the
RTOS
kernel
is
in
a
critical
section
but
cannot
make
any
calls
to
FreeRTOS
API
functions
If

in
FreeRTOSConfig
h
then
portASSERT_IF_INTERRUPT_PRIORITY_INVALID
will
result
in
an
assertion
failure
a
FreeRTOS
API
function
is

from
an

that
has
been
assigned
a
priority
above
the
configured
maximum
system
call
priority
Only
FreeRTOS
functions
that
end
in
FromISR
can
be
called
from
interrupts
that
have
been
assigned
a
priority
at
or
logically
below
the
maximum
system
call
interrupt
priority
FreeRTOS
maintains
